svg.desc: diagram id: diag-04-vertical-ai-evidence; chapter number: 2; title: Specialization Requires More Than a Wrapper; subtitle: Founder objectives, contract values, savings, prompt chains, and evaluation depth describe different parts of vertical AI.; caption: Rob Walling, Bessemer Venture Partners, Jamie Cuffe on Sequoia Capital, and Y Combinator supply these distinct reference points.; assumptions note: Units differ and bar lengths must not be read as a common ranking. For ranges reported by Rob Walling, Jamie Cuffe, and Jake Heller, typical repeats the lower endpoint solely as a plot marker; no central estimate is asserted.; note: Rob Walling's ARR range is an objective, not an outcome guarantee. Bessemer's ACV comparison and Jamie Cuffe's customer savings have different denominators. Y Combinator's evaluation example concerns a specific marketplace setting.; chart type: horizontal_bars; unit: Separate source units shown in each display; not comparable; bars: label: Walling vertical SaaS objective; min: 2; max: 20; typical: 2; display: $2–20 million ARR objective; label: Bessemer contract comparison; min: 80; max: 80; typical: 80; display: Around 80% of existing software ACVs; label: Pace customer cost savings; min: 50; max: 75; typical: 50; display: 50–75% for some insurance customers; label: Heller prompt-chain depth; min: 12; max: 24; typical: 12; display: A dozen or two dozen individual prompts; label: Gig ML marketplace evaluation; min: 10000; max: 10000; typical: 10000; display: 10,000 tailored test cases
